sentences.text: Cardiocorax is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur found in southern Angola.
This distinctive elasmosaurid possesses four unique traits known as autapomorphies.
The genus name refers to a unique heart-shaped opening between the shoulder bones.
The species name mukulu means "ancestor" in Angolan Bantu dialects.
The genus was first named by a team of researchers including Ricardo Araújo and Octávio Mateus in 2015.
A complete skull and partial postcrania attributed to the animal were found by Octávio Mateus in 2017.
The known specimens are now housed at the Museu de Geologia da Universidade Agostinho Neto in Luanda.
Fossils of Cardiocorax date to the early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 71.40 to 71.64 million years ago.
